structured_output.summary: The registry-and-remote-delivery chunk actually delivers what the plan requires: scm-sdk 0.2.2 was published and the downloaded artifact verified against both executed clean-package proofs (identical file inventory on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0), an annotated remote tag v0.2.2 peels to the published source commit 0716cfd, the delivery commit 42bcbe0 ran the exact 49-job workflow with 49/49 terminal successes, and the offline guard tools/release_delivery.py cross-binds all three receipts to the reviewed source fingerprint 519219d6. I independently re-derived the key relations rather than trusting prose: the registry receipt's archiveSha256/archiveBytes/files/vcs equal the 1.99.0 clean proof; the retained registry download and the clean package archive share digest prefix c908cad8b27863d0 in .local/artifacts; the CI receipt contains exactly 49 unique contexts that match the 24-feature x 2-toolchain matrix plus contracts-and-package parsed from .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml, all with status success and run-22 job URLs; the tag receipt's remoteRefs tie refs/heads/main to the CI commit. Negative coverage in tools/test_release_delivery.py is genuinely adversarial (missing/extra/duplicate/failed jobs, wrong run, stale sources, false summary counts, tampered registry fields, readiness provenance, publication metadata omissions, CLI refusal to fetch or write without readiness). The accepted check snapshot (59 commands, all exit_code 0, source_unchanged true) is real and bound to the same source hash. Weaknesses are evidentiary and documentary rather than functional: the current-version release-document guard passes identically whether or not its receipt-specific assertions activated (tools/test_ci.py:346-347 early-returns), and its only activated-path evidence is a self-reported receipt; the headline delivery-guard receipt records no source fingerprint or command; tag and CI observations have no producing or re-verifying tool; and RELEASE.md's publication-authorization paragraph still names only 0.1.1 and 0.2.0. No blocker or high finding; I found no fabricated or inconsistent evidence.

findings.description: test_verified_publication_is_consistent_in_current_release_documents returns early (and reports 'ok') whenever the workspace version differs from the last recorded publication version, so a passing run cannot be distinguished from a skipped one. The only recorded execution of the activated receipt-specific assertions is docs/checks/phase-20-published-document-guard.json, whose stdout is empty and whose publication_version/publication_source_commit fields are writer-supplied; the accepted 59-command snapshot (docs/reviews/phase-20-chunk-registry-and-remote-delivery-attempt-01.checks.json, checked_at 09:02:24) predates publication, and phase-status delivery_execution_constraints.qualification_snapshot explicitly instructs not to rerun the HEAD-bound gate. I verified the substance by hand (Cargo.toml 0.2.2, registry_publication 0.2.2/0716cfd, CHANGELOG.md:6 links the receipt, no obsolete-publication phrases, crates.io present in CHANGELOG/STABILITY/SECURITY), but the evidence chain itself does not prove activation.
findings.required_fix: Make activation machine-evident: have the guard emit the resolved workspace and publication versions into its report and fail (rather than silently return) when a recorded published_and_verified publication matches the workspace version but the receipt-specific block was not exercised, or add a companion assertion that the retained published-document-guard receipt exists and records the same version/source commit as phase-status registry_publication.

findings.description: The final delivery receipt records only checkedAt, passed and result. Unlike the sibling receipt docs/checks/phase-20-published-document-guard.json (which records source_sha256, command and exit_code) it does not state the source fingerprint it attests, the executed command, or a digest of the verifying tool (the registry receipt does record verifierSha256). Combined with tools/release_delivery.py:158, where the CLI defaults source_sha256 to the current fingerprint, a standalone run self-certifies its own source binding; the reviewed-source binding is only derivable indirectly because validate_receipts requires ci.reviewedSourceSha256 to equal that fingerprint.
findings.required_fix: Record source_sha256, the executed command and a verifier digest in the delivery-guard report, and either require an explicit --source-sha256 for the CLI path or print the fingerprint it resolved so the receipt is self-describing.

findings.description: The tag and remote-CI observations (docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.2.json, docs/checks/phase-20-remote-ci-run-22.json) are hand-authored JSON; no tool in the repository produces or re-reads them, so the guard can only check internal shape and cross-receipt consistency. The documented trust model covers this, but refs/heads/main and refs/tags/v0.2.2 are cheaply re-readable with git ls-remote against the authorized remote.
findings.required_fix: Add a small recorded producer/re-verifier for the tag receipt (git ls-remote against ssh://git@git-ssh.cdot.io/cdot/scm-sdk-rs.git) and for the Forgejo run/commit-status read, so these receipts have the same executed-tool provenance as the registry and package proofs.

findings.description: The publication-authorization paragraph still reads 'Maintainer authorization covers 0.1.1 and the subsequent 0.2.0 delivery recorded in the release plan', although 0.2.1 and now 0.2.2 have been published. Authorization for 0.2.2 appears only in docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:124-127, so the document that readers are pointed to for release authorization is stale.
findings.required_fix: Extend the authorization paragraph in docs/RELEASE.md to name the 0.2.1 and 0.2.2 deliveries and their authorizing plans.

findings.description: The consumer-facing publication instructions depend on repository-relative links (docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.2.json, docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.2.json) that do not resolve on crates.io or docs.rs, while lines 27-35 still foreground 0.1.1 and 0.2.0 as the installable published releases. A reader of the published 0.2.2 page is told to verify a receipt they cannot reach. This is already dispositioned as deferred in phase-status readiness03_dispositions finding 4; the packaged README is immutable for this release.
findings.required_fix: In the next qualified source change, use absolute repository/registry URLs for receipt links and state the published 0.2.2 line explicitly alongside the historical 0.1.1/0.2.0 references.

findings.description: retainedArchive conventions differ between tools: scripts/check-package.py:201 writes an absolute path (and tools/release_delivery.py:181 requires absolute for package proofs), while the registry receipt stores a repository-relative path. The final guard also re-hashes and re-extracts only the two package archives; the retained registry download (.local/artifacts/scm-sdk-0.2.2-registry-c908cad8b27863d0.crate) is never re-verified at delivery time.
findings.required_fix: Normalize the retainedArchive path convention across both tools and have release_delivery re-hash the retained registry archive against registry.archiveSha256/archiveBytes when it is present.
